historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires each cycle to preserve both logical data identity and physical bay/drive identity; device-node reuse after removal cannot be treated as the same drive.

original_test_intent: Verify five hot-remove/reinsert cycles for every approved hot-swap drive, including disappearance/re-enumeration, stable drive/bay identity, preserved file content and successful bounded writes without harming the OS, production data or array integrity.
original_method: Select only disposable approved drives, map serial/WWN to bays and storage topology, create controlled test files and hashes, have an operator remove/reinsert one quiesced drive per cycle, and capture enumeration, kernel, health, array, hash and write evidence before advancing.
manual_activity: Operator identifies the lit/labeled approved bay and physically removes/reinserts exactly one drive when instructed; automation must never infer the bay from `/dev/*` numbering.
required_inputs: Approved drive set with serial/WWN and bay map
Proof targets are not OS/boot/EFI/production or unknown
Disposable test filesystem/directory and data set
safety_requirements: Never guess a drive or bay
Exclude OS, boot, EFI, swap, mounted production and unknown devices
Do not pull an unapproved active RAID member
Resolve serial/WWN immediately before each pull
Quiesce/unmount or use the approved array procedure
Stop on I/O, hash, health, topology or rebuild anomaly
Do not advance while array is degraded or rebuilding unless explicitly specified
agent_execution_scope: Inventory serial/WWN, bay, device nodes and topology
Verify target exclusions and baseline health
Check SMART/NVMe health and error counters
Stop on anomaly and report without final verdict
engineer_actions: Provide safe detach and array procedure
Approve disposable test data and writes

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Enumeration, dmesg and RAID status are useful observations but omit the required per-drive MD5 comparison and copy test and do not prove a safe target. Generic mdadm/storcli selection may not match NVMe/HBA topology.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each approved serial/WWN and each of five cycles, record topology/health, safely detach, have the operator pull/reinsert the mapped bay, verify exact identity and controller state, compare preloaded hashes, perform a bounded approved copy/readback, and restore a healthy topology before continuing.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All available approved HDDs, different-slot reinsertion, MD5/copy checks, five repetitions and 30/30-minute timing are preserved; drive nodes, bays and storage scheme are never guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a cycle ledger keyed by serial/WWN and bay, storing pre/post topology, udev/kernel/controller events, hashes, write/readback, health and array recovery state.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds stable identity and storage-safety proof around the original physical workflow.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong-drive insertion, device-node reuse, silent data corruption, controller errors and incomplete RAID recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Hot-plug support may differ by bay/backplane/controller; file hashes do not cover untouched media and repeated array rebuilds increase wear and exposure.

project_override_considerations: The source says HDD but explicitly uses `nvme list`; media type and controller path must be resolved per slot. The private script cannot be assumed safe or applicable without a pinned reviewed revision.
expected_evidence: No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently requires repeated storage hot-plug with data-integrity checks. HDD/NVMe terminology requires topology resolution but does not create mutually exclusive intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Target identity, topology, test data and recovery are finite packages. Execution is blocked only if safe targets or recovery cannot be proven after request.

review_improvement: Prevents a generic enumeration check from replacing the mandated five-cycle content/write test and prevents accidental removal of an OS, production or unknown drive.
independent_technical_reasoning: Linux device names are unstable across hot-plug, so serial/WWN and bay identity must anchor every cycle. Data integrity requires a known preimage hash and a bounded write/readback, while safe removal depends on filesystem and RAID role. Because physical pulls are manual but monitoring and verification are automatable, and exact inputs can be supplied, REQUIRES is the correct classification.
